summary: The 2026 LLM landscape is dominated by a handful of frontier proprietary models—OpenAI's GPT series, Google Gemini, and Anthropic Claude—which together capture the vast majority of consumer web traffic and enterprise API spend. However, real-world developer adoption is increasingly shaped by cloud aggregators (AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, Google Vertex AI, Snowflake Cortex, IBM watsonx), which boost enterprise reach for models like Claude, Llama, and Mistral well beyond their direct-API footprint. Open-weight models (Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral) continue to close the benchmark gap and lead HuggingFace downloads, making the practical adoption picture far more distributed than consumer market-share data alone suggests.

models.name: GPT-5 / GPT-5.x (incl. GPT-4o legacy)
models.popularity_notes: ChatGPT held ~54-55% of worldwide AI chatbot web traffic in 2026 and OpenAI models remain the default on Azure OpenAI Service, giving them the single largest combined consumer + enterprise footprint.
models.best_for: General-purpose applications, agents, and multi-step reasoning with broad ecosystem support

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Pro / Gemini 3.x Pro
models.popularity_notes: Gemini web visits grew ~450% YoY to 2.9 billion monthly in May 2026 (~26-28% chatbot share) and it is the native model on Google Vertex AI, giving it enormous enterprise aggregator reach.
models.best_for: Long-context document and multimodal processing within the Google Cloud ecosystem

models.name: Claude Opus 5 / Claude 4.x (Sonnet & Opus)
models.popularity_notes: Anthropic leads enterprise API usage at ~40% share (Menlo Ventures) and Claude is available across AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and Snowflake Cortex, giving it the broadest enterprise aggregator reach despite only ~9% consumer web share.
models.best_for: Enterprise coding assistants and safety-critical production agents

models.name: Llama 4
models.popularity_notes: Llama remains the most-downloaded open-weight family on HuggingFace and is available on AWS Bedrock, Azure, Google Vertex AI, Snowflake Cortex, and IBM watsonx, making it the default self-hosted/open enterprise choice.
strengths: Available on every major cloud aggregator
models.best_for: Self-hosted and customizable enterprise deployments requiring open weights

models.name: DeepSeek-V3.2 / V4
models.popularity_notes: DeepSeek captured ~4% of consumer chatbot traffic and its MIT-licensed open models match frontier coding benchmarks at a fraction of serving cost, driving heavy developer adoption via OpenRouter and self-hosting.
models.best_for: Cost-sensitive high-volume reasoning and coding workloads

models.name: Qwen3 (incl. Qwen3-235B, Qwen-Max)
models.popularity_notes: The Qwen family has been adopted by over 90,000 enterprises and dominates HuggingFace open-weight downloads, especially for multilingual and on-premise coding use cases.
models.best_for: Multilingual applications and self-hosted open-weight deployments

models.name: Grok-4
models.popularity_notes: Grok holds ~2.4% of chatbot web traffic (up YoY) with deep integration into X, and is increasingly available via API and Azure, giving it growing but still consumer-skewed adoption.

models.name: Mistral Large / Mistral family
models.popularity_notes: Mistral is a leading European open/commercial option available on AWS Bedrock, Azure, Google Vertex AI, Snowflake Cortex, and IBM watsonx, giving it strong enterprise aggregator reach for efficiency-focused workloads.

models.name: GPT-oss (120b / 20b)
models.popularity_notes: OpenAI's open-weight GPT-oss models deliver strong performance at low cost and have seen rapid HuggingFace and OpenRouter adoption as a self-hostable alternative to the proprietary GPT API.
models.best_for: Low-cost self-hosted deployments wanting OpenAI-family compatibility

models.name: Microsoft Phi-4
models.popularity_notes: Phi-4 is a leading small-model choice for high-performance reasoning in constrained deployments, distributed natively through Azure AI Foundry and widely downloaded on HuggingFace.
models.best_for: Edge and resource-constrained deployments needing strong reasoning per parameter
